newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM palladium ends higher, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM palladium ends higher, others mixed.

text.p: Tokyo palladium futures ended higher on Thursday, backed by continued delays in Russian metal exports to Japan, while other precious metal futures ended mixed after drifting sideways, traders said.

The spot April palladium contract expired at noon, ending up 13 yen per gram, with 88 lots of deliveries. Other prices ranged from five yen to 11 yen up, with benchmark February up eight yen at 608 yen.
"Backed by Russia's continued suspension of exports, market players were willing to take the small number of deliveries at the spot expiry," one trader said.

The physical palladium market has been getting tighter on the Russia factor, while the physical platinum market has been little affected by Russia's suspension of metal exports as the shortage can be filled by South Africa.
Traders said a large overhang of palladium short positions may lead to volatile trading early next month after Japan's "Golden Week" holidays.
After lacklustre trade, gold futures ended slightly firmer on the back of the yen's weakness, while platinum was mixed as profit-taking capped the topside.
Gold prices ranged from two yen to seven yen per gram up.
Benchmark February gold was up seven yen at 1,380 yen.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $340.20/70 per ounce at 0737 GMT, against $341.10/60 in New York on Wednesday.
Traders were wary of taking fresh positions in the gold market ahead of the G7 meeting on Sunday that may determine the direction for the currency market.
Benchmark February platinum was down one yen at 1,469 yen.
Benchmark February silver was up 0.7 yen per 10 grams at 194.9 yen.
